nodes.label: Coherence
nodes.intent: The repository-level reading surface: configuration, package contract, generated maps, and the authored explanation of why the harness exists.

nodes.label: Harness core
nodes.intent: Composes configuration, public commands and shared contracts into the Coherence CLI.

nodes.label: Source adapters
nodes.intent: Translate language syntax and platform configuration into the common graph vocabulary consumed by the harness core.

nodes.label: Coordination
nodes.intent: Combines work ownership, dependencies, consequences and trusted evidence into the next action an agent owes.

nodes.label: Source derivation
nodes.intent: Reads source and specs into the shared graph of components, symbols, claims and imports.

nodes.label: Diagnostics and ratchets
nodes.intent: Measures change, risk sites, architectural coupling and evidence gaps against the repository and its recorded baselines.

nodes.label: Durable evidence
nodes.intent: Records decisions, defects, experiments and verification history so later sessions can recover what was observed and decided.

nodes.label: Agent lifecycle
nodes.intent: Connects supported agent hosts to repository controls, lifecycle instructions and attributable activity traces.

nodes.label: Reading surfaces
nodes.intent: Projects existing models into context packets, diagrams, component maps and inspectable reading surfaces.

nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.intent: Classifies repository subjects against a shared catalog and preserves caller-assessed evidence, ambiguity and staleness.

nodes.label: Verification
nodes.intent: Evaluates declared claims against structural checks and named test evidence, refusing missing or incomplete proof.

nodes.label: Executable contracts
nodes.intent: Exercises the harness through focused unit contracts and end-to-end fixtures built from the same public data shapes that consuming repositories use.

links.subject: src/derivation/derive.ts#buildGraph
links.because: The containment oracle checks deepest declared ownership without fabricating dependency edges. This addresses ownership preservation in the graph projection, not completeness of every adapter or source construct.

links.subject: src/evidence/decisions.ts#readTrustedJournal
links.because: The strict journal projection validates surviving records and refuses the whole reading on damage. This addresses the invalid-input refusal part of the boundary obligation, not all caller-visible failure semantics.
problems: Assessment expired: changed or missing: package.json; changed or missing: src/types.ts

links.subject: src/evidence/status.ts#recordVerify
links.because: The merge preserves the dated prior oracle verdict when a later run skips it. This addresses retained report history, not immutable evidence or complete crash recovery.
problems: Assessment expired: changed or missing: package.json; changed or missing: src/evidence/status.ts; changed or missing: src/types.ts

links.because: SessionStart reads readTrustedJournal before projecting durable decisions. It requires damage to refuse the verdict-bearing projection instead of silently presenting a partial journal as trusted.
Reading surfaces consume the derived graph to show component ancestry and imports. They require containment to follow the deepest declared ancestor without inventing dependency connections.
runVerify publishes scoped and fast results through recordVerify. A skipped oracle must retain its prior dated verdict rather than erase the evidence used by subsequent readers.
